abstract: Insulin plays a crucial role in lowering glycemia, but it is also a powerful anabolic hormone with potent effects on the vasculature. Most studies on insulin vascular actions have focused on endothelial cells. Much less is known about its effects on the mural cells of the microvasculature known as pericytes. This gap in knowledge is particularly relevant for the pancreatic islet microvasculature which is exposed to high insulin levels and relies on local pericytes to efficiently deliver its glucoregulatory hormones. To investigate how insulin affects islet pericyte function and the impact on glucose homeostasis, we generated mice that lack insulin receptors in pericytes (PerIRKO). Loss of insulin signaling in pericytes raised insulin levels, induced islet expansion and beta cell proliferation in the pancreas and in intraocular islet grafts from PerIRKO mice. These changes in beta cell numbers were accompanied by increased islet vascular density, although capillaries were dysfunctional ex vivo, compromising islet hormonal responses to an intravenous glucose challenge. Our study supports that insulin itself regulates islet endocrine and vascular niches through previously unrecognized actions on pericytes, revealing a novel mechanism that links the vasculature to endocrine homeostasis.
